A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that 5-aminolaevulinic acid (5-ALA)-based fluorescence-guided resection of spinal tumors is feasible and safe.
we have shown that 5-aminobenzoylaminolevulinat acid-induced fluorescence is a sensitive and specific technique for the diagnosis of malignant spinal tumors.
the 5-aminolaevulinic acidity (ALA)-induced fluorescence (5-ALF) is certainly a highly effective tool in the differential analysis and histopathological classification of spinal tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
5-aminolaevulinic acid (5-ALA) fluorescence-guided surgery is a safe, feasible, and reliable tool for the resection of spinal tumors.
the use of 5-ALA in spinal tumor surgery is safe, and that the fluorescence signal is useful in the surgical treatment of spinal tumors, particularly when used with the 532-nm laser.
the 5-ALA-induced fluorescence in spinal tumors is not only a marker of malignant tumors, but also a marker of tumor progression.
